nodes.name: Execute Workflow Trigger
nodes.notes: T2/design.md: two callers pass { chat_id, text } here -- telegram-adapter.json (replies) and assistant-scheduler.json (proactive pushes). Same 'shared seam, multiple callers' justification llm-gateway.json already established.

nodes.name: Call sendMessage
nodes.notes: Bot token read from the n8n environment variable TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN (never hardcoded, never an n8n credential -- same custody convention as DRAFT_WEBHOOK_SECRET/RESYNC_WEBHOOK_SECRET; a Code node isn't needed here since the HTTP Request node's expression editor reads $env directly). parse_mode='HTML' lets callers use <b>/<i> for the digest pushes' light formatting; plain text is valid HTML-mode input too, so slash-command replies need no escaping changes. options.response.fullResponse + neverError=false mirrors llm-gateway.json's 'Call Gemini generateContent' -- a non-2xx status makes the node genuinely fail and enters n8n's native retry (maxTries=2), rather than being swallowed as normal response data.

nodes.name: Return result
nodes.notes: T2's Notes: converges to a single terminal leaf, per design.md's Grounding sources (L29's terminal-branch-convergence lesson) -- this sub-workflow is called with waitForSubWorkflow: true by both future callers, and llm-gateway.json's own 'Return result' node exists for exactly the same reason (n8n's sub-workflow completion signal raced on asymmetric terminal branches in a prior live incident). There is only one branch here today, but the node is added preemptively so a later failure branch (e.g. a distinct 'chat not found' path) has something to converge onto rather than requiring a refactor under pressure.

parameters.content:
## Telegram Send

Reusable sendMessage sub-workflow. Two callers: telegram-adapter.json (replies to inbound questions) and assistant-scheduler.json (the four proactive pushes). Contract: { chat_id, text } in, { success, message_id? , error? } out -- never throws.

See .specclaw/changes/012-assistant-bot/design.md, Architecture + File Changes Map, and tasks.md T2.

### Placeholders to fill in on import

- **TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN** n8n environment variable -- the token @BotFather issues for this bot (see docs/setup/assistant-bot-setup.md). Never store it as an n8n credential; the HTTP Request node reads it directly via $env in its URL expression.
- Callers (telegram-adapter.json, assistant-scheduler.json) invoke this workflow by name (cachedResultName: 'Telegram Send') with workflowId.value left blank -- re-point each caller's Execute Workflow node at the real imported workflow via the resource picker once this file is imported, same convention every prior phase's sub-workflow references use.
